newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Motta says scandal politically motivated.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Motta says scandal politically motivated.

text.p: Communications Minister Sergio Motta, at the eye of a corruption scandal rocking Brazil, said Friday accusations he may be tied to an alleged congressional vote-buying scheme are politically motivated.
"I don't recognize any of the accusations against me. There's not one proven fact," Motta told reporters in Rio de Janeiro, where he was attending a telecommunications forum.

Folha de Sao Paulo daily, citing taped phone conversations, alleged this week that five lawmakers took bribes to vote in favor of a bill that would allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to stand for a second term next year.
The paper also printed stories linking Motta to the alleged cash-for-votes scam.

On Friday, Motta said those quoted in the transcripts "are people linked to other political interests" and threatened to sue them for libel if they repeat suggestions he was involved in the alleged scam.
Motta said Folha's publication of allegations "was a criminal act (that) created a climate of insecurity in financial markets," adding he wants a thorough investigation of the matter.
Asked if he believed Cardoso's would-be opponent in the 1998 presidential race, former Sao Paulo mayor Paul Maluf, was behind the scandal, Motta responded: "It's really too early to say that."

A staunch party loyalist and long-time friend of Cardoso's, Motta denied his continued presence on the Cabinet hurts the government. "This doesn't effect anything. Everything continues as normal," he said.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom 5521 5074151))
